title: Goods and Services Tax Voucher Fund (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Goods and Services Tax Voucher Fund (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: GST Voucher Fund purpose
sections.summary: The Fund's main purpose is to provide financial assistance to the less well-off to offset part of their GST expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The main purpose of the Fund is to provide financial assistance to the less well-off, to offset part of their GST expenses.

sections.label: Amendments to GST Voucher Fund
sections.summary: Amendments expand the Fund's purpose beyond the less well-off, allowing it to fund the Assurance Package for GST and grants-in-aid for infants and children.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Amendments to Part 2 of the Act expands the purpose of the GST Voucher Fund, such that the beneficiaries are no longer confined to those who are less well-off.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With this amendment, the GST Voucher Fund can then be used to fund the Assurance Package for GST, which will benefit all Singaporeans during the transition period.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The amendments will also allow assistance to be provided in the form of grants-in-aid, to defray the expenses incurred by parents or guardians for infants and children under their care and charge.

sections.label: Concern over broadening purposes
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned that broadening the Fund's purposes moves away from its original intent of financing relief from GST to low-income Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The concern I have with this amendment is that in broadening the purposes of the GST Voucher Fund to "mitigate the impact of the goods and services tax", we are moving away from the original intent that the GST Voucher Fund is meant to directly finance "relief from goods and services tax" to low-income Singaporeans.

sections.label: Question on policy intent
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister whether the Government still intends to use the Fund to provide cash and cash-equivalent GST relief to lower income households.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is a lot easier to point to the cash value of the GST Voucher payouts, and then compare that to the GST paid by individuals, rather than to count up the value of other subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I wish to ask the Minister whether the Government continues to have the policy intent of using the GST Voucher Fund, as far as possible, to provide cash and cash-equivalent relief from GST to lower income households.

sections.label: Net GST paid shares
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance revealed that the bottom 40% pay 10% of net GST, while the top 20% and foreigners pay 60%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance has revealed in this year’s Budget debate that the bottom 40% only pay for 10% of net GST.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The top 20% and foreigners pay for 60% of net GST.

sections.label: GSTV Fund establishment
sections.summary: The GSTV Fund was established to help lower income Singaporeans cope with their GST expenses, mitigating GST's regressive nature.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The GSTV Fund was established to help lower income Singaporeans cope with their GST expenses, mitigating GST’s regressive nature.

sections.label: Foreign workers in Singapore
sections.summary: As of June 2019, Singapore had 1.4 million foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As of June 2019, there were 1.4 million foreign workers in Singapore.

sections.label: FDW economic contribution
sections.summary: A 2019 regional study found FDWs contributed S$11.1 billion in 2018, or 2.4% of Singapore's GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a 2019 regional study, FDWs contributed S$11.1 billion to the economy in 2018, or 2.4% of Singapore’s GDP.

sections.label: Bangladeshi workers' salaries and debt
sections.summary: A 2014 study reported Bangladeshi workers earn $350 to $800 but may pay up to $15,000 in recruitment fees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2014 study reported that Bangladeshi workers earn the lowest salaries – between $350 and $800 – and yet they could pay up to $15,000 in recruitment fees which are 26 to 51 times their monthly wage that leaves them in crippling debt.

sections.label: Bangladeshi workers' food quality
sections.summary: A 2015 NUS and HealthServe survey of 500 Bangladeshi workers found 80.6% said caterer food was of poor quality.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many have experienced food that they feel is of poor quality and inadequate for their nutritional needs, confirmed in a 2015 survey by NUS and HealthServe of 500 Bangladeshi workers – 80.6% indicated "the food I get from the caterer is of poor quality".

sections.label: Food price increase
sections.summary: Food prices rose about 7% faster than inflation over 10 years, with some essentials at least 60% more expensive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Overall, price of food has increased approximately 7% faster than inflation over the past 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Certain food essentials have become at least 60% more expensive.

sections.label: GST Vouchers for migrant workers
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Minister will consider distributing GST Vouchers to migrant workers and reviewing support schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the Minister consider distributing GST Vouchers to migrant workers as well as reviewing social support schemes for them?

sections.label: GST help for lower income
sections.summary: There is a standing commitment to regularly help lower income Singaporeans with GST expenses through the GST Voucher scheme, plus an Assurance Package for the transition to a higher GST rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First, we have a standing commitment to provide more help to lower income Singaporeans for their GST expenses on a regular basis, that is, through the existing GST Voucher scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On top of that, we plan to support all Singaporeans during the transition to a higher GST rate through the Assurance Package for GST.

sections.label: Enhancing permanent GST Voucher scheme
sections.summary: When the GST rate is increased, the permanent GST Voucher scheme will be enhanced to continue meeting this commitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: When the GST rate is increased, we will enhance the permanent GST Voucher scheme to continue to meet this commitment.

sections.label: Foreign work pass holders GST
sections.summary: Foreign work pass holders pay the increased GST rate from the onset, while Singaporeans effectively see a delay of at least five years after offsets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Like all foreign work pass holders, they will have to pay the increased GST rate from the onset, compared to Singaporeans, who will effectively see a delay in the GST increase for at least five years after offsets.
